title: Verdict
description: What a refuter concluded about one finding. Binary on purpose: there is no confidence scale, because a scale is where a refuter hedges. A claim falls on evidence, not on doubt: `undecided` lets the claim through to the reader, marked, and records that nothing settled it. The refuter must quote code for its verdict, checked by the same anchoring guard the finding passed - a refutation nobody can check is worth no more than a finding nobody can check.

reason.description: Why, in one or two sentences, tied to the code you quote below.

evidence_line.description: 1-indexed line in the numbered file that carries your evidence.

evidence_snippet.description: The code that settles it, copied verbatim. When the verdict is `stands`, quote the code you tried and failed to refute; when it is `undecided`, the code that left it open.

glossary.stands: I tried to kill it and could not - the claimed inputs do reach that code and do produce that consequence
glossary.not-reachable: no input reaches that code path, so the claim is about dead ground
glossary.already-handled: the check the finding says is missing is present, above or around the quoted line
glossary.misread: the code does not do what the finding says it does
glossary.wrong-location: something real, but not at this line - the quoted code is not where it happens
glossary.no-consequence: the described situation occurs and nothing observable follows from it
glossary.intended: the behaviour is deliberate and consistent with the code around it
glossary.undecided: what you were given does not settle it either way - not enough to show the claim holds, nothing that shows it fails
